newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank wants money rates above 5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank wants money rates above 5 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank is determined to keep short-term interest rates above five percent, bank vice-governor Liang Cheng-chin said on Monday.
"The central bank's determination to keep the short term interest rates above five percent remains unchanged," Liang told reporters after the money market's Monday close.

Liang was responding to an interest rate slide that brought the overnight rate below five percent Monday for the first time in weeks. The rate traded for most of the day below the 5.0 percent level and ended at 4.958 percent.
Liang did not say what the central bank might do to ensure short-term interest rates do not fall further, but the bank has been acting persistently to keep the rates stable.
The bank on Monday issued T$8 billion in three-month negotiable certificates of deposit to absorb excess liquidity in the money market, the latest in a series of such issues.
Central bank officials said Monday's issue had an average yield of 5.195 percent.
In October and November, Taiwan's overnight and short-term commercial paper rates were persistently below five percent, dipping at times below 4.5 percent.

The central bank responded by setting five percent as a benchmark target and issuing short-term debt from time to time, but has not taken stronger measures such as reversing recent decreases in the rediscount rate or reserve requirements.

Officials have said the bank wants to strike a balance between the interests of depositors, who do not want rates to fall too low, and the state's desire to keep enough liquidity available to fuel a hoped-for fourth-quarter economic recovery.
